rimsky documentation index

Rimsky is a reactive node-graph orchestration platform. You write a template
that declares nodes, what each node subscribes to, and what claims it takes;
you deploy the template and create an instance; rimsky dispatches work as
state changes cascade through the graph. Your executors do the work.

This file lists every document rimsky ships. Each line gives a path and the
question that path answers. Every path is relative to docs/. Fetch the files
your task needs and nothing else.

Pick by task:
  Learning the model            concepts.md, then capabilities.md
  Writing a template            templates.md, cookbook/, examples/
  Calling rimsky from code      http-api.md, mcp.md, cli.md
  Implementing a service        protocols/, then grpc.md
  Running a deployment          operating.md, config.md, env-vars.md, images.md
  Diagnosing a failure          errors/, cookbook/journey-stale-node.md,
                                cookbook/journey-stuck-instance.md


ORIENTATION

  README.md — What rimsky is, how its public surface fits together, and which document answers which question.
  llms.txt — This index: what documentation exists and which file answers which question.
  concepts.md — Definitions of the 75 nouns rimsky's own surfaces use, and where you meet each one.
  capabilities.md — What rimsky does at this release, which surface reaches each capability, and where the behaviour differs from a reasonable reading of the surface.


REFERENCE: THE SURFACES YOU DRIVE

  cli.md — Every rimsky CLI verb, its arguments, its flags, and what it does.
  http-api.md — Every route of the control API, the supervisor's async-callback listener, and the sensor-webhook ingress, with method, path, request shape, response shape, and auth posture.
  mcp.md — Every MCP tool and resource the control API exposes at /v1/mcp, and how to drive rimsky from an MCP client.
  templates.md — Every key of the template and of the compose manifest, what each declares, and how the keys compose.
  permissions.md — All 49 permission actions and all 6 bundled roles, and which actions each role grants.


REFERENCE: THE SURFACES YOU CONFIGURE AND RUN

  operating.md — Which deployment posture to choose, how the three role processes find each other, and what the deployment tells you when something wedges.
  config.md — Every key of rimsky.yml, the supervisor config, the CLI config, the CLI alias files, and each bundled producer's file, with type, default, and effect.
  env-vars.md — Every RIMSKY_* environment variable the shipped code reads, which process reads it, its default, and its effect.
  images.md — Every published image, what it runs, the commands it accepts, the paths it reads and writes, and the ports it opens.
  packages.md — Which Go modules, npm packages, and release archives rimsky publishes, and how to depend on them.
  licensing.md — Which part of rimsky ships under Apache-2.0, which under AGPL-3.0-or-later, and what each license asks of you.


REFERENCE: THE PROTOCOLS YOU IMPLEMENT

  grpc.md — Every RPC and message shape in the ten .proto files, and where to get the definitions.
  protocols/README.md — Which guide to read for the protocol you are implementing.
  protocols/conventions.md — The conventions every rimsky protocol shares: the wire definitions, the HTTP+JSON bridge, and mTLS enrollment.
  protocols/executor.md — How to implement Executor and ExecutorObservability so rimsky can run a node's work through your service.
  protocols/claim-producer.md — How to implement ClaimProducer and ClaimProducerObservability so rimsky can hand a node exclusive access to something outside rimsky.
  protocols/data-processing.md — How to add versioned staging to a claim producer with the DataProcessing mix-in.
  protocols/validation.md — How to implement Validation so your service rejects bad templates at registration rather than at dispatch.
  protocols/publisher.md — How to implement Publisher so external events wake instances, and how a sensor kind fits that shape.
  protocols/lifecycle-subscriber.md — How to answer the seven callbacks that report template, instance, and run-scope state changes.
  protocols/host-agent.md — How to write your own host agent that dials rimsky's proxy and runs work on a developer's machine.
  protocols/events.md — The declared shapes of rimsky's event-log rows and cascade signal payloads, for a consumer of the event log or an author of a signal predicate.
  protocols/conformance.md — How to prove your service against the protocol contract with rimsky conformance.


COOKBOOK: PROBLEM SHAPES AND JOURNEYS

  cookbook/README.md — Which recipe or journey covers the problem you have.
  cookbook/queue-worker.md — How one node takes the next item from a store, processes it, and removes it.
  cookbook/fan-out-over-a-store.md — How one claim becomes one dispatch per item without the template enumerating the items.
  cookbook/claim-handoff.md — How several nodes work on one acquisition that resolves exactly once, at the end.
  cookbook/park-and-resume.md — How a node waits out a rate-limited upstream instead of failing or burning retries.
  cookbook/error-routing.md — How to give different failures different answers, and why fail-fast is the floor.
  cookbook/iterative-convergence.md — How to run a node on its own output until a declared condition holds.
  cookbook/message-driven-wake.md — How work starts from a schedule, a webhook, a polled change, or a node's own send.
  cookbook/sub-graph-delegation.md — How to make a whole graph one named step of a calling graph.
  cookbook/journey-zero-config.md — How to get from an empty machine to a node at terminal/success with no configuration.
  cookbook/journey-split-roles-postgres.md — How to get from an empty network to three role containers over one Postgres database.
  cookbook/journey-stale-node.md — Why a node did not re-run, and how to read each of the six causes.
  cookbook/journey-stuck-instance.md — Why an instance never reaches terminal, and which four reads find the run that has not settled.


ERROR CATALOG

  errors/README.md — Which page covers the literal error-class string you are holding.
  errors/routing.md — How the runtime looks an error class up in a node's error_types map and runs the action it finds.
  errors/acquire.md — The five acquire/ classes raised before dispatch, while the runtime opens a node's claims.
  errors/abandoned.md — What settles a run under abandoned, the class for claim work that was thrown away.
  errors/runtime-dispatch.md — The three classes the runtime raises when it cannot reach an executor, the call runs past its deadline, or the answer breaks the protocol.
  errors/runtime-attributes.md — The four classes the runtime raises while building a node's attribute bag and checking it against the executor's schema.
  errors/infra-faults.md — The dispatch faults error_types cannot route.
  errors/spawn-failed.md — spawn_failed and the other classes the host-agent proxy raises for a late-bound local binary.
  errors/agent-classes.md — The thirteen agent/ classes the bundled claude-agent executor advertises.
  errors/http-node-classes.md — The nine http/ classes the bundled http-node executor advertises.
  errors/verifier-classes.md — The five verifier/ classes, and which bundled verifier declares which.
  errors/http-api-rejections.md — The synchronous rejections the control API returns to a caller before any work starts.
